title: Hashing
summary: Map and Set, frequency counts, prefix-sum hashing, top-k

guide.title: The most useful speed-up in interviews
points: Many brute-force answers ask "is this value somewhere else?" with a second loop: O(n²).
A hash set or map answers that in O(1) on average, so the whole solution becomes O(n).
Two sum, duplicates, anagrams, frequency counts and caching are all hashing.

guide.title: Hashing in real systems
points: Caches (Redis, browser cache) and database indexes find a record by key without scanning everything.
Duplicate detection: cloud drives spot the same file uploaded twice; mailing tools remove repeated e-mails.
Trending hashtags and top searches are frequency counts followed by "top k".
Payment reconciliation matches each debit with its credit: the same idea as two sum.

guide.title: Key → bucket
points: A hash function turns a key into a bucket number, so lookup goes straight to the right place.
Set: only keys ("have I seen it?"). Map / dictionary: key → value ("how many times?", "at which index?").
Average O(1) per operation; many keys in one bucket (collisions) can make it slower.

guide.title: Look for the other half
points: Two sum: for each x, check whether target − x was seen before; if not, remember x and its index.
One pass, O(n) time, O(n) memory, instead of trying every pair.

guide.title: Frequency, prefix sums, top-k
points: Frequency: count first, then answer (first unique character, anagram check, majority element).
Prefix-sum hashing: a subarray sums to k when prefix[r] − prefix[l] = k. Count earlier prefix sums equal to sum − k; start with sum 0 seen once.
Top-k: count, then sort the (value, count) pairs, or keep a heap of size k for O(n log k).

guide.title: What goes wrong with maps
points: JavaScript plain objects turn keys into strings (1 and "1" collide); use Map for real keys.
Arrays and objects as keys compare by reference, not by content. Join them into a string key instead.
Java: Integer values above 127 must be compared with equals(), not ==.
C++: map is ordered and O(log n); unordered_map is the O(1) average one. Reading count[x] also inserts x.

guide.title: For advanced learners and interviews
points: Hashing vs sorting: sorting is O(n log n) with no extra memory; hashing is O(n) with O(n) memory. Say the trade-off.
Design classic: an LRU cache is a hash map plus a doubly linked list, giving O(1) get and put.
Rolling hashes compare substrings fast; Bloom filters answer "probably seen" with very little memory.
Next step: Stack and Queue, for "most recent first" problems.

problems.title: Contains duplicate
problems.statement: Return true if any value appears at least twice.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: A hash set is smaller than the array when there are repeats.

problems.title: Two sum
problems.statement: Return the 0-based indices (smaller first) of two elements that add to target. Exactly one answer exists.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Store value -> index; look for target - value first.

problems.title: First unique character
problems.statement: Return the 0-based index of the first character that appears only once, or -1.
problems.hint: Count every character, then scan again.

problems.title: Count anagram groups
problems.statement: Words that are anagrams belong to one group. Return the number of groups and the size of the largest group.
problems.hint: The sorted letters of a word are a good key.

tests.input: eat tea tan ate nat bat

hiddenTests.input: pat tap apt top pot now

problems.title: Longest consecutive run
problems.statement: Return the length of the longest run of consecutive integers present in the array (any order). Aim for O(n).
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Start counting only at values whose predecessor is missing.

problems.title: Top k frequent
problems.statement: Return the k most frequent values, most frequent first. For equal counts, the smaller value comes first.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Count, then sort by count and value.

problems.title: Subarrays with sum k
problems.statement: Return how many contiguous subarrays have a sum equal to k. Values can be negative.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Count earlier prefix sums equal to sum - k.
